subject: Performance SLO: p95/p99 latency targets (hosted vs current provider) - post-call recap
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Chen <sam.chen@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO: p95/p99 latency targets (hosted vs current provider) - post-call recap

Hi Sam -

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we're all aligned: 

Call recap:
- Finlytics current end-to-end latency targets & constraints: you mentioned user-facing chat product with streaming; p95/p99 targets are key for SLA discussions.
- Key metrics we need from you for a fair apples-to-apples benchmark: request/response size distribution, current provider p95 & p99 (end-to-end), throughput (req/s), expected concurrency, and any network egress patterns.
- Streaming: you confirmed server-sent-chunk streaming for chat (we should test both streaming and non-streaming).

What we need from Finlytics (action items):
1) Share the most recent metrics CSV (p95/p99, percentiles, request sizes) - you mentioned current_provider_metrics.csv.
2) Capture a representative 10-15 minute trace (if possible) or provide a synthetic workload profile (concurrency/arrival pattern). network_trace.pcap or a brief description is fine.
3) Confirm acceptable test window (we suggested Jun 17-18) and whether we can get temporary test credentials or an API sandbox.

What Redwood will do next:
- Draft a short test plan and run a hosted API benchmark vs your supplied metrics. We'll focus on end-to-end p95/p99 (including network + client-side overhead where possible), throughput at target concurrency, and streaming behavior.
- Share a simple script you can run locally (or we can run from our test harness) and produce a comparison report.

Proposed targets (initial):
- Hosted Redwood target: p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 700ms (end-to-end) for your typical short chat completions (payloads ~500 tokens). These are initial goals; will adjust based on your workload.

Attachments: I'll attach the test plan draft and please attach your CSV/pcap.

Would you be able to share the CSV and confirm the test window?

Thanks -
Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment(s): redwood_test_plan.pdf (stub)

From: Sam Chen <sam.chen@finlytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO: p95/p99 latency targets (hosted vs current provider) - post-call recap

Hi Laura -

Thanks for the recap - appreciate the clear next steps. See answers inline: 

- Current provider (third-party infra) end-to-end (client -> provider -> model -> client): p95 = 420 ms, p99 = 1,280 ms (these are across our production mix).
- Average throughput: ~200 req/s sustained during peak; peak bursts up to ~350 req/s for ~2-3 minutes.
- Typical concurrency: ~50 concurrent active chats; expected growth in next quarter to ~80.
- Payload sizes: short chats ~200-600 tokens; long-form ~1,200 tokens (we primarily care about short-chat latency).
- Streaming: yes - we use chunked SSE for UI; per-chunk size ~80-120 tokens. We'll want streaming to be tested.

Attached: current_provider_metrics.csv (per-minute percentiles for the last 7 days) and a short PCAP we captured during a peak window (network_trace.pcap).

Test window: Jun 17-18 works for us. We'll provision temporary sandbox keys - I'll send a secure link for the creds.

One clarifying question: are Redwood's hosted numbers quoted end-to-end or just server-side processing? We want to ensure comparisons include network + library overhead if possible.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Chen
Head of Infrastructure, Finlytics
sam.chen@finlytics.com

---
Attachment(s): current_provider_metrics.csv, network_trace.pcap

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Chen <sam.chen@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO: p95/p99 latency targets (hosted vs current provider) - test plan & next steps

Hi Sam -

Perfect, thanks for the files. We reviewed the CSV and PCAP - helpful. A few clarifying points and what we'll run during the Jun 17-18 window:

Planned Redwood hosted benchmark (summary):
1) End-to-end latency tests (client-side script -> Redwood hosted API -> complete response delivered): we'll run both streaming and non-streaming modes to measure p95/p99. This will include network + client SDK overhead where we can (we'll run the client script from a region close to your users per the PCAP).
2) Throughput and concurrency scaling: ramp to sustained 250 req/s and bursts to 400 req/s, with concurrency sweeps at 25/50/80.
3) Payload mix: mirror your production mix (short 60%, medium 30%, long 10%).
4) Metrics and artifacts we'll deliver: percentile latency CSVs, flamegraphs for server compute, kv-cache hit rates, and a short recommendations write-up (batching, cache policies, quantization options).

Questions for Finlytics before we start:
- Confirm the exact tokenization model (so we match payload sizes client-side).
- Can you provide a single IP range we should expect from your test clients, or should we run from multiple egress IPs?

Quick note on your question about what Redwood numbers represent: for our hosted benchmark we'll produce both server-side processing latencies (model+runtime) and end-to-end measurements (including client-side and network). We'll label them clearly so you can compare to your current-provider CSV.

I'll attach the short test plan (redwood_test_plan.pdf) with step-by-step scripts. We'll follow up with a simple curl/python harness and an optional k6 load spec if you prefer.

Sound good? If so we'll queue infra and request a temporary higher-concurrency trial key for Jun 17 morning.

Best,
Laura

---
Attachment(s): redwood_test_plan.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Performance SLO: p95/p99 latency targets (hosted vs current provider) - internal ops notes

Laura / Aditya -

Notes for ops:
- Prioritize test run on hosted clusters in us-west region (closest to their users per PCAP).
- Use model variant: redwood-open-7b-quant (same tokenization as their current model); confirm tokenization with Finlytics before run.
- Enable streaming path (we need to validate backpressure + chunking behavior) and capture per-chunk latency.
- Request trial key with concurrency cap of 200 for the test window (we can throttle client side).
- Tag results with deal_id=DEAL-2397 and include in next weekly pipeline sync.

I'll loop in SRE if we need ephemeral capacity. Aditya, can you provision the trial creds and the k6 script?

Thanks,
Marissa
VP, Solutions & Revenue Engineering

From: Sam Chen <sam.chen@finlytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@finlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO: p95/p99 latency targets (hosted vs current provider) - test creds & schedule

Hi Laura / Marissa -

All set for Jun 17-18. We won't be able to share long-lived keys; instead we'll provision temporary sandbox credentials valid for 48 hours. I'll post the secure link to the creds in our SSO vault and also share a one-time-download link via the secure channel.

A couple of quick clarifications before your run:
- Tokenization: we're using the standard cl100k_base tokenization for the model in short chat mode.
- Network egress: tests coming from a small set of office IPs (I'll share the CIDR block in the secure note). If you need us to originate traffic from other IPs, we can coordinate.
- Success criteria: if Redwood can demonstrate end-to-end p95 at or below ~300ms and p99 below ~800ms for the short-chat mix at concurrency=50, we'll consider it a strong signal for moving forward to a pilot. Any longer and we'll have to discuss tradeoffs (quantization vs cost vs accuracy).

We'll upload the temporary creds and the CIDR to the secure link by EOD today. Looking forward to the results.

Best,
Sam

---
Note: temporary credentials and CIDR will be shared via our SSO vault link (not included inline).
